findings.title: The runner never clears .test-build, so compiled tests from deleted, renamed or other-branch sources keep running

serves.scenario: The two bug cards each need a 'fails first, then passes' reading from this runner. A compiled test left in .test-build/test-node/ by one card's branch still runs after the .ts source is renamed, deleted or absent on another branch, because findTests walks whatever .test.js is on disk and tsc never removes orphaned output. The gate then reads a 'not ok' and a nonzero exit (or an extra 'ok') for a test that does not exist in the tree under test.

findings.rubric: c1 / tr-01: exits 0 when the tests pass and nonzero when one fails. Smallest fix: remove .test-build (rmSync with recursive and force) before spawning tsc.
findings.reproduction: 1. Add test-node/tmp.test.ts containing a failing test. 2. Run npm run test:node; it exits nonzero as expected. 3. Delete test-node/tmp.test.ts. 4. Run npm run test:node again. tsc succeeds, but .test-build/test-node/tmp.test.js is still found and run, so stdout has 'not ok' and the exit is nonzero although every test in the source tree passes.
findings.label: f1

replies.restate: The runner kept stale compiled tests in .test-build after sources were deleted.
replies.verify: Added rmSync of .test-build before the tsc compile; reran the repro and only the live smoke test runs.

findings.title: package-lock.json looks hand-edited: one root line added, no resolved @types/node entry in the diff, so npm ci on a clean clone is unproven

serves.scenario: The spec goal is a developer running npm run test:node on a clean clone after npm ci. The lock diff adds only the root devDependencies line for @types/node@^24.10.2 and no packages entry; the card expected about 20 lines. The root lock entry also still lists @types/jest and jest, which the package.json hunk does not show, and an npm-regenerated lock would have dropped them. If the lock has no node_modules/@types/node entry satisfying ^24.10.2, npm ci fails as out of sync; if @types/node is not installed at the root, tsc fails on types:["node"] and no test can run. I cannot see the rest of the lock, so this is a risk to confirm, not a proven failure.
